metadata.case_name: PANG KWAI WAH v. TSANG KWONG WING

injuries.description: Removal of right eye / severe right eye injury (enucleation) with prosthesis fitted
source: fragments of the lens entered his right eye".
the eye was so badly damaged that it had to he removed and a prosthesis fitted in its stead.
injuries.icd_description: Ocular laceration or rupture with prolapse or loss of intraocular tissue, unilateral

source: during which, according to the medical reports, he was treated for a lacerated eyelid and ruptuted eyeball.
injuries.icd_description: Open wound of eyelid or periocular area

injuries.description: Sympathetic reaction in left eye (secondary involvement requiring further hospitalization)
source: the severe trauma to his right eye gave rise to a sympathetic reaction in his left eye, which necessiated future-hospitalization for a further 4 days in July.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of eye or orbit

manifestations.description: a great deal of pain from his right eye
pain to a lesser degree from his left eye
his right eye continued to be painful and phthisical
regular visits to his doctor for treatment to relieve the discomfort of the prosthesis
his right eye socket weeps frequently each day
loss of depth perception caused by his monocular vision
my eyesight is not as wide as ordinary people (reduced peripheral vision)
difficulty in hitting the ball or shuttlecock; sporting activities now only infrequently

treatments_received: admitted to hospital immediately after the assault for a period of 10 days (treated for a lacerated eyelid and ruptuted eyeball)
future-hospitalization for a further 4 days in July for sympathetic reaction in left eye
re-entered hospital in October 1986 where his right eye was removed
treatments_future: replacement prostheses (three replacements in round figures)
ongoing medical follow-up/maintenance of prosthesis and eye-socket at $400 per annum

losses.description: Loss of right eye (enucleation) and replacement by prosthesis
Occasional displacement of the prosthesis when wiping the tears from that eye so that only the white of his 'eye' is visible; cosmetic effect (minimal but subjectively significant)

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: loss of confidence socially; fear of being treated as a 'monster' and concern about how people will react
The Plaintiff said 'I think this will affect my marriage prospects'

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Sporting activities (badminton and tennis) are severely curtailed; now plays only infrequently because of difficulty hitting the ball or shuttlecock
his social life is generally at a low ebb

comparable_cases.injury_description: loss of sight in one eye (plaintiff did not have the eyeball removed; more cosmetic disfigurement; longer hospitalization)
